summary: Academic sweep (Nov 2026) of 11 families compatible with intraday futures prop firms and FTMO Swing. 36 candidates catalogued; 8 judged worth pre-registered tests, led by (1) the ES overnight drift 02:00-03:00 ET (RFS 2023; 1.48 bps/day gross, mechanism-based, persisted to 2020; net viability hinges on today's lower relative tick cost and conditioning on prior-day selloffs), (2) month-end Treasury index-extension buying traded intraday into the 4pm strike in ZN/ZB (Hartley-Schwarz Sharpe~1 in cash; NY Fed shows 20% of month-end volume in 10 minutes around 4pm), (3) USD appreciation into the WMR 4pm London fix with month-end equity-hedging amplification in 6E/6B/6A (Krohn-Mueller-Whelan JF 2024; Melvin-Prins), (4) Tokyo 9:55 gotobi fix in 6J, (5) EIA crude/natgas and (6) WASDE post-release continuation, (7) option-expiration pinning in ES extended to the 0DTE era, and (8) dealer-gamma regime switching between intraday mean reversion and momentum. Negative/closed-by-evidence: FX intraday momentum, Goldman-roll front-running, pre-announcement drift (procedure changes), OPEX/day-of-week/crypto weekday effects, 1-min cross-market lead-lag and LOB deep learning (data/latency). Decay literature implies ~50% post-publication haircut (more in US liquid markets) and abrupt death when institutions change; a single strategy therefore needs post-cost OOS Sharpe >=3 or a portfolio of >=5 independent sleeves to deliver net 1.5. Most candidates are honestly LOW plausibility for net Sharpe 1.5 on their own; the realistic path is a portfolio of mechanism-anchored, time-stamped flow trades.

decay_evidence.summary: Published anomalies lose roughly half their in-sample performance out of sample; decay is fastest for high in-sample Sharpe (overfitting), for recently published strategies, and in the most arbitraged market (US). Mechanism-based intraday edges die abruptly when the underlying institution changes (fix window 2015, lock-up reforms 2014/2020, gold auction 2015, LETF pre-hedging, Bloomberg strike move 2021) rather than fading gradually.

findings.paper: McLean & Pontiff 2016, 'Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?', Journal of Finance 71(1)
findings.result: 97 anomalies: returns 26% lower post-sample/pre-publication and 58% lower post-publication; decay larger for high in-sample returns and for cheap-to-arbitrage stocks.

findings.paper: Falck, Rej & Thesmar 2022, 'When do systematic strategies decay?', Quantitative Finance 22(11):1955-1969 (WP 'Why and how systematic strategies decay', arXiv 2105.01380)
findings.result: 72 published strategies (US 1963-2014, intl 1995-2018): OOS performance about 50% of in-sample; publication year explains ~30% of decay variance (newer decays faster, ~5pp/yr); overfitting proxies (in-sample Sharpe) add ~15%; arbitrage proxies marginal.

findings.paper: Jacobs & Muller 2020, 'Anomalies across the globe: Once public, no longer existent?', Journal of Financial Economics 135(1)
findings.result: 241 anomalies in 39 countries: significant post-publication decline only in the US; no reliable decline elsewhere -> arbitrage (not data mining) drives US decay; expect fastest decay in US liquid futures.

findings.paper: Chen & Zimmermann 2020, 'Publication Bias and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns', Review of Asset Pricing Studies 10(2)
findings.result: Bias-adjusted expected returns only ~12% below in-sample for published predictors; the much larger post-publication drop (~50%+) is therefore mostly real decay (mispricing correction), not selection bias.

findings.paper: Harvey, Liu & Zhu 2016 RFS '...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns'; Harvey & Liu 2021 JFE 'Lucky Factors'
findings.result: Multiple testing implies t>3.0 hurdle for new findings; bootstrap-based 'lucky factors' procedure to control false discoveries across many tested variants.

findings.paper: Hou, Xue & Zhang 2020 RFS 'Replicating Anomalies'; Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen 2023 JF 'Is There a Replication Crisis in Finance?'
findings.result: HXZ: 65% of 452 anomalies insignificant with value weights/no microcaps. JKP: Bayesian hierarchical model - most factors replicate, work OOS in 93 countries, but posterior alphas are shrunk and post-publication alphas lower (not zero).

findings.paper: Suhonen, Lennkh & Perez 2017, 'Quantifying Backtest Overfitting in Alternative Beta Strategies', Journal of Portfolio Management 43(2)
findings.result: 215 bank systematic strategies: live Sharpe about 27% of backtest Sharpe (median haircut ~73%).

findings.paper: Mechanism-shutdown cases found in this sweep
findings.result: Pre-announcement drift (Kurov) tied to pre-release procedures changed 2013-2014; WMR fix reversals shrank after Feb-2015 5-minute window (FCA OP46); London gold fix leakage ended with ICE electronic auction Mar-2015; LETF end-of-day effects weakened as intermediaries pre-hedge (Barbon et al. 2022); Goldman-roll front-running unprofitable after 2004 (Dubois-Marechal); Treasury index strike moved 3pm->4pm Jan-2021 (NY Fed); 0DTE daily since May-2022 changed gamma dynamics.

implied_haircuts.published_in_sample_to_live_us_liquid_fu: multiply gross in-sample Sharpe by 0.4-0.5 (publication decay) then subtract costs; for strategies with in-sample Sharpe > 2 assume additional overfitting haircut (0.3x).
implied_haircuts.practitioner_backtest_to_live: 0.25-0.5x (Suhonen et al.; Bailey-Lopez de Prado deflated Sharpe).
implied_haircuts.required_backtest_bar: to credibly deliver net Sharpe 1.5 live, a single pre-registered strategy needs post-cost OOS Sharpe >= 3 (t>3 with >= 300 trades), or a portfolio of >= 5 weakly correlated mechanism-based sleeves each with net OOS Sharpe >= 0.6.
implied_haircuts.regime_rule: treat any institutional change date as a hard sample split; evidence before the change does not count toward OOS.

prompt_rules: Treat every published in-sample Sharpe as an upper bound; apply a 0.5x publication haircut and full costs before deciding whether a candidate can reach net Sharpe 1.5.
Pre-register each test: paper's exact rule, parameters, window, instruments, IS/OOS split and success threshold written to a file before the first backtest; one OOS evaluation per registered variant.
Prioritise edges with an identifiable forced trader and a verifiable timestamp: fix windows, index strike times, auction results, LETF rebalancing, option expiries, European open.
Split every sample at institutional change dates (2015-02 fix window, 2015-03 gold auction, 2021-01-14 Treasury strike, 2022-05 daily 0DTE, 2014 lock-up reforms); only post-change data counts as OOS.
Convert all timestamps to exchange/local time with explicit DST handling (ET, London, JST, CET) and verify event times against the official calendars.
Model costs as >=1 tick plus commission per side, add slippage for market orders at 02:00 ET, opens and settlements; require the edge to survive 2x costs.
Report gross edge in ticks per trade; drop any rule averaging under 2 ticks per trade unless n>=500 and win rate above 58%.
Spend Databento first on ohlcv-1m for ES, NQ, ZN, 6E, 6J, CL, GC, ZC 2018-2026 including overnight sessions; buy tbbo only for a 3-month ES sample to validate BVC order-flow proxies.
Flag any variant of a CLOSED family and test it only if the construction is materially different (new asset class, new window, new conditioning data) and documented as such.
Control multiple testing across all variants with Harvey-Liu t>3 or deflated Sharpe; log every test, including failures, in a running registry.
Build the portfolio from several small mechanism-based sleeves (overnight drift, month-end Treasury strike, FX fixes, EIA/WASDE continuation) rather than one dominant strategy.
Size positions with intraday realized-vol targeting so forecast daily P&L vol is at most one third of the prop firm's daily loss limit; never scale up in low-vol regimes beyond base size.

Check instrument availability per firm before testing: Treasury and grain futures only at futures firms; DAX/FTSE/Nikkei/HSI only via FTMO CFDs; overnight-session trades allowed at futures firms if flat before the daily close.
